definition: Showing great care and close attention to every small detail.
example: The museum's meticulous restorers spent a year cleaning a single tapestry thread by thread.
nuance: Meticulous praises careful attention to detail, while fastidious often suggests fussiness or being hard to please.
prompt: A baker is preparing a cake for a regional baking competition.
options: The meticulous baker weighed each ingredient to the gram before mixing.
The meticulous baker tossed in flour by the handful and hoped the cake would rise.
The meticulous baker was so frightened of the judges that her hands shook nonstop.
The meticulous baker left smears of frosting on the plate and never noticed them.
reasons: Measuring everything precisely shows close, careful attention to detail.
Rough guessing is the opposite of careful precision.
The word describes carefulness, not fear or nervousness.
Overlooking obvious messes contradicts careful attention to detail.

practice.prompt: A student is writing a research paper for a history class.
options: His meticulous paper was typed the night before and never proofread at all.
The meticulous report was so long that it filled three thick binders.
She was meticulous about the due date, so she forgot it entirely.
Her meticulous notes listed the page number for every quotation she used.
reasons: Rushing and skipping revision shows no attention to detail.
Length alone says nothing about how carefully the work was done.
Forgetting a deadline is the reverse of being careful about it.
Recording each source detail exactly reflects thorough care.
